name: Flex
description: Flex builds other companies' products: it designs, engineers and manufactures electronics for networking and communications, consumer lifestyle products, industrial and automotive equipment and medical devices, and runs the supply chain behind them, earning a thin margin (about 5 to 6 percent segment margin) on very large volume. Its fastest-growing business is Cloud and Power Infrastructure, which makes rack-level compute systems, power equipment and liquid cooling for data centres and AI, with 24 percent of sales and about 9 percent margin. No customer is over 10 percent of sales and the ten largest are 45 percent. On 2026-05-05 Flex announced it will split off Cloud and Power Infrastructure as a separate listed company.

employees.note: Approximately 150,000 employees including contractor workforce (149,686 in the 10-K table); more than 100 facilities in about 30 countries.

businessLines.name: Integrated Technology Solutions (ITS)
businessLines.how: Contract manufacturing and supply-chain services for communications, high-speed networking, enterprise and satellite equipment and for lifestyle products: customers' product designs are built and shipped, so Flex earns a thin margin on large pass-through volume plus design and engineering fees.

businessLines.name: Regulated Manufacturing Solutions (RMS)
businessLines.how: Contract manufacturing for regulated, safety-critical products (industrial and energy equipment, automotive compute and power electronics, medical devices and drug delivery): multi-year programmes with qualification and compliance work, earning a thin per-unit margin on volume.

businessLines.name: Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI)
businessLines.how: Designs and builds integrated compute systems, liquid cooling, and rack- and facility-level power systems for hyperscale cloud, colocation and enterprise data centres: large systems-level programme orders from a small number of hyperscale customers, with higher engineering content than pure assembly.

brands.name: Nextracker (former subsidiary)
brands.note: Spun off to Flex shareholders on 2024-01-02; not in current figures.

whatsNext.when: announced 2026-05-05; targeted first quarter of calendar 2027
whatsNext.text: Tax-free spin-off of the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment into an independent publicly traded company (the rest of Flex keeps ITS and RMS); subject to board, shareholder and Singapore High Court approval and SEC requirements; the 10-K says there is no assurance it will occur
